findings.summary: Exact ScienceWorld distribution identity can be bound by PyPI SHA256 even where an observed Git tag is absent; package-to-source-commit attribution still needs byte-level binding.
For online memory, same initial DB is insufficient for strong same-M replay; pre-retrieval state, task/update history, retrieval config/query and ordered member identities/digests must also match.
MemCompiler Table-3 'same retrieved M' supports a fixed-candidate-pool delivery intervention but cannot be upgraded to selected-identity replay without evaluated memory/run artifacts.
Exact public SpeedRunner code implements allow_replay as a staged-copy admission switch: static no-replay commit versus same-record replay all-pass commit/failure rollback.
Same nominal ScienceWorld problem ID is weaker than same replay state; exact environment identity plus state/replay-equivalence evidence is needed for strong replay proof.

Current public SpeedRunner files do not make Figure 12 numerically replayable: public replay/non-replay configs are not a one-field task-3 pair, run artifacts are ignored, ScienceWorld is unpinned and ASI replay tests/results are not durably emitted.
Persistent empty-codebook ResultCache can reuse a complete outcome while its key lacks explicit runner revision, environment artifact/JAR, dataset-record digest and backend/server fingerprint.

A cached outcome and an independent replication are different statistical objects; cached traces are counted in current evaluation scores, so independent replication must explicitly bypass memoized outcome reuse.
AutoMat exposes rich evaluator evidence but path-addresses the observed files; re-evaluation can read changed bytes at the same path unless a snapshot/content-addressing discipline is imposed.
AutoMat --archive is not explicitly a self-contained copy of the resolved agent artifact directory; thin archival should bind every external object by immutable digest/content-addressed locator.

Later AutoMat re-evaluation of the same artifact directory can expose prior repro_evaluation_results.json/repro_eval_prompt.txt because all files are listed/readable; primary independent review should exclude evaluator-generated bytes.

AutoMat's blinded SME calibration (n=40, quadratic-weighted kappa 0.69, within-one accuracy 0.80) materially supports benchmark-scale approximate judgment in the tested scope but not final scientific authority.
Judge calibration is revision-specific; old calibration cannot automatically transfer across evaluator code/model/prompt/rubric/input-exposure drift or out-of-scope domains/claim types.

Calibration input protocol is part of judge identity: SMEs were blinded to final answer/self-evaluation/judge assessment while current automated evaluation can receive agent self-assessment, so agreement is not a matched-input interchangeability experiment.

Numeric provenance is not semantic claim provenance. OmniScientist's host-skill documentation explicitly acknowledges same-number/wrong-quantity passability; quantitative authority must bind typed output quantity/field/unit, not global numeric membership.
Gate authority is implementation-edition specific. OmniScientist CLI has latest-success/script-hash/entry-hash/citation/perception hardening that the Claude Code host gate does not share.

OmniScientist CLI integrity tests directly establish intended invalidation of changed-script and failed-latest numeric evidence, but flattened value membership still leaves quantity identity unresolved.

The OmniScientist Claude Code host skill numeric membership predicate reads stdout numbers from all ledger entries without returncode or current-script invalidation, so failed/stale recorded values remain membership-eligible in that edition; no published exploitation is alleged.

The first observed packaged OmniScientist release v0.1.0 postdates arXiv v1 by three days; release artifact hashes identify distributions but do not identify the paper's evaluated run absent an explicit run/revision binding.
